title: The Flea and the Man
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Flea bit a Man, and bit him again, and again, till he could stand it no longer, but made a thorough search for it, and at last succeeded in catching it. Holding it between his finger and thumb, he said--or rather shouted, so angry was he--"Who are you, pray, you wretched little creature, that you make so free with my person?" The Flea, terrified, whimpered in a weak little voice, "Oh, sir! pray let me go; don't kill me! I am such a little thing that I can't do you much harm." But the Man laughed and said, "I am going to kill you now, at once: whatever is bad has got to be destroyed, no matter how slight the harm it does."
Do not waste your pity on a scamp.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Flea do to the Man again and again?
options: Fly around his head
Steal small crumbs from his table
Bite him
Hide inside his coat

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man finally succeed in doing?
options: Catching the Flea
Chasing the Flea outside
Trapping the Flea in a jar
Convincing the Flea to leave

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man demand to know from the Flea?
options: Where the Flea came from originally
How many other fleas are hiding nearby
Why the Flea chose him instead of someone else
Who the Flea is, that it makes so free with his person

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Flea beg the Man to do?
options: Give it back its freedom tomorrow
Let it go and not kill it
Trade it for a different flea
Hand it over to someone kinder

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does the Flea give for why it should be spared?
options: It promises never to bite anyone again
It claims to have bitten him by accident
It is such a little thing that it can't do much harm
It offers to repay him for the trouble

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man decide to do with the Flea?
options: Kill it now, at once
Release it far from his home
Keep it as a curiosity
Give it to a neighbor's child

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Man unmoved by the Flea's plea about its small size?
options: He does not believe the Flea is really so small
He is too angry to listen to any argument at all
He thinks the Flea is lying about its own size
He believes something harmful should be destroyed regardless of how little harm it does

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Man's shouting suggest about how he feels before catching the Flea?
options: He is only mildly annoyed by the whole situation
He has been provoked to real anger by the repeated bites
He is trying to frighten off other insects nearby
He is amused rather than upset by what happened

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Flea "whimpered" its plea?
options: It shouted as loudly as it could
It laughed nervously while speaking
It spoke in a weak, frightened voice
It refused to speak at all

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Something harmful does not deserve mercy just because it seems small
Small creatures should always be forgiven for their mistakes
Anger is never a good reason to punish anyone
It is wrong to search too hard for something that bit you

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man do before catching the Flea?
options: He calls for help from a neighbor
He waits quietly until it bites again
He examines his skin for marks
He makes a thorough search for it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Man hold the Flea once he catches it?
options: Inside a small glass jar
Between his finger and thumb
Wrapped in a handkerchief
Pinned beneath his boot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Flea feel once it is caught?
options: Confident
Amused
Terrified
Indifferent

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Man ask the Flea who it is before deciding its fate?
options: He wants to express his anger before delivering his judgment
He genuinely does not know what kind of creature bit him
He is hoping the Flea will name an accomplice
He plans to let it go if it answers politely

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what principle does the Man apply that goes beyond just this one Flea?
options: That every creature deserves a chance to explain itself
That mercy should always be shown to the weak
That anger should never guide an important decision
That harmful things deserve destruction regardless of their size

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Flea made "so free" with the Man's person?
options: It moved very quickly across his skin
It took liberties without any right to do so
It asked politely before biting him
It stayed in one place without moving

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Man decides to let the Flea go after it apologizes
A Flea convinces the Man that it never bit him
A Man refuses to spare a Flea despite its plea that it is harmless
A Man and a Flea agree to leave each other alone
